plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Add to QQQI, targeting 15%, to favor income and broad index exposure.
Trim CRWD to 5% to reduce single name concentration.
Buy MSFT, targeting 10%, as a top-quality name from the scanner.
Maintain a large cash buffer for capital preservation.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, but still carries market risk, especially from broad index exposure.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce broad index concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Buy TZA, targeting 4%, to add some inverse market exposure for balance.
Add to QQQI, targeting 10%, to increase income exposure.
Keep total adds within total trims plus a cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration, blending broad index with quality tech and some inverse exposure. Market downturns could still impact returns.

plan: Add to SOXL, targeting 6%, and SPAL, targeting 6%, to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Buy TZA, targeting 6%, and SOXS, targeting 5%, as high-scoring inverse setups.
Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer and use wider but strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and high-scoring scanner setups, which significantly increases both potential upside and drawdown. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can lose a lot very quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to prioritize income and covered-call exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to cut high-beta single names and sector exposure.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability and prioritize low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes steady monthly distributions from income ETFs and low drawdown. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market selloffs, so this is not a savings account.
